title: Van Gogh Painting Sells for $190.4 Million (He Never Made a Cent From It)
description:
Vincent van Gogh's "Chestnut Trees in Blossom" (Chataigniers en fleurs) sold for $190.4 million with fees at Sotheby's New York on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, a new auction record for the artist.

The facts:
- He painted it in May 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, just outside Paris, a few days after he arrived there. He died two months later, on July 29, 1890.
- It never sold while he was alive: after his death it went to his brother Theo, then to Theo's widow Jo, who sold it in 1905.
- The old Van Gogh auction record was $117.2 million for "Orchard with Cypresses" in 2022. The new one is about $73 million higher.
- The owners, the Blaquier-Arrieta family, had owned it since 1975. A claim by the heirs of an earlier owner was settled before the sale.

human_angle: The record isn't the story; the gap is: the painting earned its painter exactly nothing (it was never sold while he lived, it went to his brother), and 136 years later it beat his own record by $73 million. The kid holding up her drawing at the end is our point: nobody can tell what art is worth while the artist is alive.

questions.q: How much did the Van Gogh painting sell for in November 2026?
questions.a: Chestnut Trees in Blossom (Chataigniers en fleurs, May 1890) sold for $190.4 million with fees at Sotheby's New York on Nov. 18, 2026, a new auction record for Van Gogh.

questions.q: What was the previous Van Gogh auction record?
questions.a: $117.2 million for Orchard with Cypresses, sold in 2022 from the Paul Allen collection. The 2026 sale beat it by about $73 million.

questions.q: Did Van Gogh make money from Chestnut Trees in Blossom?
questions.a: No. He painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in May 1890 and died two months later. It passed to his brother Theo and then to Theo's widow, who sold it in 1905.
